messages.body_plain:
Rajiv, Thank you for the followup and for your kind words. For future reference, its important to remember that any files or subdirectories that are in your application directory will be uploaded to the ShinyApps servers. It is advisable to remove unnecessary files and directories for faster upload, and the ensure the total application size does not exceed the current 100Mb limit. Also, as I have mentioned before, we will likely increase the max application size after the ShinyApps alpha has ended. Thanks -Andy On Thu, Apr 3, 2014 at 10:28 PM, Rajiv Shah wrote: > I worked with Andy to solve this error. The problem was that the total size of all my files was over 100 MB. I had a data folder with csv and RDA files. The csv files were the original data with the RDA having the slimmed down data that my app needed. Dear all,

thank you for your previous answers, I've found what the problem was and have solved it: in order to do that, I needed to see the logs of the shiny-server (AFAIK, not possible to see from the ShinnyApps interface). There, I found that the function stat_summary_hex() needs the 'hexbin' package that is not automatically instantiated. Including at the beginning of the script a line with:

library(hexbin)

solved the problem. (I needed to install that package, too)

I wonder why hexbin is not instantiated automatically, but just in case someone else run into the same problem, the approach mentioned above could help.

Cheers,

messages.body_plain:
H Tareef,

I teach at a small college where we are beginning to write shiny apps for instructional purposes.  I am pleased with shinyapps so far, and I have some suggestions about pricing for academic institutions.

As you know, a shinyserver app opens only one R session at a time.  For some of the apps we write, this is no problem:  many people can be in on the same R session and the only problem is that the app may appear to respond a bit slowly.  However ,some instructional apps keep a record of previous user actions, so that when two or more people are in on the same R session the record-keeping devices in the server.R program end up combining the records of all users.

Hence from our point of view, it would be great to have a system where the app can run multiple sessions, one per user.  At a school my size, you might have 25 sessions at once when the entire class is using the app, and this would occur rarely.  If there were some way to provide a substantial educational discount for a service with the option of multiple R sessions, I certainly would lobby to get my school to pay for this valuable service.

Regards,
Homer White

Note:  Of course the shiny apps can be run locally, but we have not yet been able to do this on the College's RStudio server (which is how our students use R).
